claims.text: Peds: start insulin when T2DM presents more severely (A1C > 8.5%): glargine, detemir or premixed insulin;
claims.quote: Insulin is also initiated in children who present with more severe type 2 diabetes (HbA1C > 8.5% [> 69 mmol/mol]) (3); glargine, detemir, or premixed insulin can be used.

claims.text: DKA or HHS: USU IV insulin first, then SC; start metformin once acidosis resolves.
claims.quote: Children with DKA or HHS usually require intravenous insulin initially and then are transitioned to subcutaneous insulin (3). Once acidosis resolves, metformin can be initiated.
claims.locator: Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes in Children and Adolescents › Pharmacologic treatment › Insulin

claims.text: Lispro (Humalog): inject SC w.in 15 min b4 a meal or STAT after a meal.
claims.quote: Administer HUMALOG ® U-100 or U-200 by subcutaneous injection into the abdominal wall, thigh, upper arm, or buttocks within 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after a meal.
Hypoglycemia is the most common adverse reaction associated with insulins, including LANTUS.

claims.text: All insulins shift K+ into cells, possibly causing hypokalemia.
claims.quote: All insulins, including LANTUS, cause a shift in potassium from the extracellular to intracellular space, possibly leading to hypokalemia.

claims.text: BBs, clonidine: signs of hypoglycemia may be ↓ or ⍉.
claims.quote: Antiadrenergic Drugs ( e.g., beta-blockers, clonidine, guanethidine, and reserpine ): Signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia may be reduced or absent.

claims.text: TZDs: fluid retention and HF; watch for HF and consider reducing or stopping the TZD.
claims.quote: Fluid retention and heart failure with concomitant use of thiazolidinediones (TZDs) : Observe for signs and symptoms of heart failure; consider dosage reduction or discontinuation of TZD if heart failure occurs.

claims.text: Check glucose more often w chgs in dose, other drugs, meals or activity, and in renal or hepatic impairment or hypoglycemia unawareness.
claims.quote: Increase frequency of glucose monitoring with changes to: insulin dosage, concomitant drugs, meal pattern, physical activity; and in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and hypoglycemia unawareness.

claims.text: Monitor K+ in pts @ risk of hypokalemia.
claims.quote: Monitor potassium levels in patients at risk of hypokalemia and treat if indicated.

claims.text: Learn to recognize and mgnt hypoglycemia.
claims.quote: Patients and caregivers must be educated to recognize and manage hypoglycemia.
Rotate injection sites to reduce risk of lipodystrophy and localized cutaneous amyloidosis.

claims.text: Don't mix glargine w other insulin.
claims.quote: Do not dilute or mix LANTUS with any other insulin or solution.
Never share a LANTUS SoloStar prefilled pen, insulin syringe, or needle between patients, even if the needle is changed.

claims.text: Check the insulin label b4 each inj.
claims.quote: instruct patients to always check the insulin label before each injection

claims.text: Severe hypoglycemia can cause sz and may be life-threatening.
claims.quote: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizures, may be life-threatening or cause death.

claims.text: Untx hypokalemia may cause resp paralysis, ventricular arrhythmia and death.
claims.quote: Untreated hypokalemia may cause respiratory paralysis, ventricular arrhythmia, and death.
